resources.string: Remote Viewfinder for Samsung Wi-Fi cameras
The camera asks whether to allow this phone. Confirm on the camera (it asks every time Remote Viewfinder starts).
Tap Join camera Wi-Fi and start Wi-Fi → Remote Viewfinder on the camera, in either order: finderscope waits for the camera\'s network and joins it.
To remember your camera\'s network, so the next connection needs no confirmation, Android needs the location permission. finderscope uses it only for that, and for GPS tags if you switch them on.
The camera is ready about 5 seconds after it shows its Cancel button. finderscope keeps looking for up to a minute.
The camera network was not found or not accepted. Is Remote Viewfinder on? If Android does not list it, join it in the phone\'s Wi-Fi settings: finderscope connects when you come back.
The phone is not on a camera network. Pick the camera\'s network (AP_SSC_…) in the Wi-Fi settings.
No camera at hand? The demo runs a simulated camera on this phone.
Filled in from the Wi-Fi. Change it only if the camera uses another one.
Enter the camera\'s address, for example 192.168.102.1
Hold to focus, release to take the picture. Slide off to cancel. The volume keys work too.
No app to show the picture
Could not focus, no picture taken
The card\'s folder numbering is used up. Format the card or use another one.
The camera could not take the picture. Try again.
The camera took the picture but did not hand it over. It is on the card.
The picture is on the camera\'s card.
The camera did not do that: %1$s
The live view was interrupted and is back.
Preview %1$s saved to Pictures/finderscope. The full picture stays on the card.
Copy every picture to the phone
Into Pictures/finderscope. The 2012 models hand over a small preview only; the full picture stays on the card.
Tag pictures with the phone\'s location
The position goes into the copy on the phone. The camera\'s own file on the card stays without it: the cameras ignore a position sent to them. Needs the location permission.
finderscope is an independent open-source project. It has no relation to Samsung Electronics and is neither endorsed nor supported by them. Camera names only say which cameras it works with.

resources.string: Stay connected in the background: off
While finderscope is not on screen the camera stays connected for this long, so you can switch apps without the camera leaving Remote Viewfinder. Off: disconnect right away.
The camera\'s Wi-Fi is gone (camera switched off or out of range).
Hold to focus: press the shutter to focus, let go to take the picture
Tap to focus: tap the picture to focus, the shutter takes the picture
With tap to focus, a tap on the live view focuses and keeps the focus; tap again to focus anew. The shutter then takes the picture with it, or focuses and takes it in one go when nothing was focused.
Take the picture. Tap the live view first to focus.
Start Remote Viewfinder on the camera. finderscope joins its network as soon as it appears (up to 3 minutes).
No camera network appeared within 3 minutes. Is Remote Viewfinder on? If the phone does not see it, join it in the Wi-Fi settings: finderscope connects when you come back.
